narrative:
The model estimates a 64% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors about your professional profile.

Your relatively short overall work experience of 1-5 years was the strongest factor pulling the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expects to stay, only about half have similarly limited experience, while the rest tend to have six or more years. This limited tenure signals higher turnover risk to the system.

The fact that you have received other job offers while working here was the second most important driver and pushed the prediction strongly toward leaving. Most employees the model predicts will stay do not report receiving outside opportunities.

Your employment in the “other” sector, rather than medical or education, was the third notable influence and also nudged the outcome toward departure. Only about 22% of employees expected to stay work in this broader category.

Although several other aspects of your situation, such as lack of a bonus, no medical insurance, and feeling you have not received deserved recognition, likely added to the risk, the model weighed your limited experience, external opportunities, and sector most heavily.

The organization should consider discussing retention strategies with you, such as clearer promotion paths, better rewards, or additional training. You may want to reflect on whether your current role still aligns with your longer-term goals given the external opportunities available to you.
